title: Vacanze e viaggi
sub: Past simple e past continuous - raccontare il weekend
grammar: Past simple (regolari e irregolari), past continuous, when e while
situation: Raccontare il weekend a un collega

lessons.title: Raccontare al passato
lessons.intro: In italiano per il passato usi quasi sempre il passato prossimo («sono andato», «ho visto»). In inglese, per dire quando è successo qualcosa, serve il past simple. Qui impari a raccontare una vacanza senza cadere nelle trappole più comuni.

steps.title: Past simple: azioni finite nel passato
steps.body:
Si usa per azioni **concluse**, spesso con un'indicazione di tempo passato: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago.

**Verbi regolari**: base + **-ed**.
- walk -> walked, visit -> visited
- con -e finale solo -d: live -> lived
- consonante + y: study -> studied (ma play -> played)
- una sillaba breve con una consonante: stop -> stopped
- in inglese britannico: travel -> **travelled**

**Negative e domande**: si usa **did / didn't + verbo base**. Il verbo base non prende MAI il passato: l'ausiliare lo porta già.
table: Was it good? / Were you there?
ex: We stayed in a small hotel near the station.
Siamo stati in un piccolo albergo vicino alla stazione.
Did you enjoy the trip?
Ti è piaciuto il viaggio?
They didn't travel by plane.
Non hanno viaggiato in aereo.

steps.title: Verbi irregolari: vanno studiati
steps.body: I verbi irregolari non fanno -ed. I più usati in viaggio:
ex: I lost my phone on the train.
Ho perso il telefono sul treno.
We got to the hotel at midnight.
Siamo arrivati in albergo a mezzanotte.

steps.title: Attenzione: passato prossimo italiano, non present perfect
steps.body:
Quando racconti qualcosa che è successo **in un momento preciso** (ieri, sabato scorso, nel 2022) in inglese usi il **past simple**, anche se in italiano diciamo «sono stato», «ho visto».

- «Ieri sono stato a Roma.» -> **I was in Rome yesterday.** (non «I have been to Rome yesterday»)
- «Sabato ho visto un film.» -> **I saw a film on Saturday.**

**Errori tipici degli italiani**:
- «Did you went...?» / «She didn't went...»: dopo did/didn't il verbo è alla base -> **Did you go...? / She didn't go...**
- «goed», «buyed», «eated»: sono forme inventate -> **went, bought, ate**
- «I am been in London»: mai am/is/are + participio -> **I was in London.**
ex: Did you go to the beach on Sunday?
Sei andato in spiaggia domenica?
I didn't see the castle.
Non ho visto il castello.

steps.title: Past continuous e while / when
steps.body:
Il **past continuous** (**was / were + verbo in -ing**) descrive un'azione **in corso** in un momento del passato, lo «sfondo» della storia (in italiano spesso l'imperfetto: «stavo dormendo»).

- I **was sleeping** at ten o'clock. (stavo dormendo)
- They **were walking** along the beach.

Si usa insieme al past simple: l'azione lunga è al continuous, quella breve che la interrompe è al simple.
- **While** we **were having** lunch, it started to rain.
- It started to rain **when** we **were having** lunch.
- I **was walking** home **when** I met an old friend.

**While** si usa con l'azione lunga (past continuous). **When** si usa soprattutto con l'azione breve (past simple), ma può introdurre anche l'azione lunga.
Attenzione: se un'azione ne segue un'altra, usa il simple: **When** I arrived, I called Anna.
ex: While I was packing, my taxi arrived.
Mentre facevo la valigia, è arrivato il taxi.
We were waiting for the bus when it started to snow.
Aspettavamo l'autobus quando ha iniziato a nevicare.

steps.s: Last summer we ___ to Greece.
steps.it: L'estate scorsa siamo andati in Grecia.
steps.why: «Go» è irregolare: past simple went. «Goed» non esiste.

steps.s: I ___ my passport at home yesterday.
steps.it: Ieri ho lasciato il passaporto a casa.
steps.why: Con «yesterday» serve il past simple, e leave è irregolare: left.

steps.s: ___ you enjoy the film last night?
steps.it: Ti è piaciuto il film ieri sera?
steps.why: Domanda al past simple: Did + soggetto + verbo base.

steps.s: We didn't ___ the museum because it was closed.
steps.it: Non abbiamo visitato il museo perché era chiuso.
steps.why: Dopo didn't il verbo è alla forma base.

steps.s: I was sleeping when the phone ___ .
steps.it: Dormivo quando è suonato il telefono.
steps.why: Ring è irregolare (ring - rang). L'azione breve che interrompe è al past simple.

steps.s: While we ___ dinner, the lights went out.
steps.it: Mentre cenavamo, è andata via la luce.
steps.why: Azione in corso nel passato con soggetto we: were + -ing.

steps.q: Come si dice «Ieri sono stato a Roma»?
opts: I have been to Rome yesterday.
I am been in Rome yesterday.
steps.why: Con un tempo preciso (yesterday) si usa il past simple di be: was. Il present perfect non va con yesterday.
Dopo didn't il verbo torna alla forma base: go, non went.

steps.q: Scrivi la forma giusta del verbo tra parentesi
steps.s: We ___ (buy) some souvenirs in the market.
steps.why: Buy è irregolare: bought.

answers: I was sleeping when you called
I was sleeping when you phoned
I was sleeping when you rang
I was sleeping when you called me
I was sleeping when you phoned me
I was sleeping when you rang me
I was asleep when you called
I was asleep when you phoned
I was asleep when you rang
steps.why: Azione in corso (imperfetto italiano) interrotta da una breve: was sleeping + past simple.

steps.s: I dropped my phone ___ I was running for the bus.
steps.why: L'azione lunga (was running) si introduce con while; anche when è possibile.

steps.s: Where ___ last weekend?
steps.why: Domanda al past simple: did + soggetto + verbo base.

steps.s: Yesterday I have visited the castle.
steps.why: Con yesterday serve il past simple, non il present perfect.

steps.s: Did you went to the beach on Sunday?
answers: Did you go to the beach on Sunday
steps.why: Dopo did il verbo è alla base: go.

steps.s: We were walk along the river when it started to rain.
answers: We were walking along the river when it started to rain
steps.why: Il past continuous vuole il verbo in -ing: were walking.

steps.s1: I didn't have a good time at the party.
steps.why: Negativa al past simple: didn't + verbo base.

steps.s1: The phone rang while I was in the shower.
steps.why: While + past continuous per l'azione in corso: while I was having a shower.

steps.it: Non abbiamo visto nessuno al museo.
steps.en: We didn't see anyone at the museum
alts: At the museum we didn't see anyone

lessons.title: Il lessico delle vacanze
lessons.intro: Le parole per organizzare un viaggio, muoversi in aeroporto e raccontare cosa hai fatto in vacanza. Molte entreranno nel ripasso a intervalli.

ex: I packed my suitcase the night before.
Ho fatto la valigia la sera prima.
Don't forget your passport!
Non dimenticare il passaporto!
I took my camera to the mountains.
Ho portato la macchina fotografica in montagna.
Our luggage arrived two hours late.
I nostri bagagli sono arrivati con due ore di ritardo.
words.note: Non numerabile: mai «luggages». Si dice a piece of luggage.

ex: The flight to Dublin takes two hours.
Il volo per Dublino dura due ore.
There was a long delay at the airport.
C'è stato un lungo ritardo in aeroporto.
words.note: «Ritardo» di un mezzo = delay. Anche verbo: The train was delayed.

ex: We booked the hotel online.
Abbiamo prenotato l'albergo online.
words.note: Anche nome: a book = un libro. Prenotazione = booking.

ex: Accommodation in the city centre is expensive.
L'alloggio in centro è caro.
words.note: Non numerabile e con due c e due m.

ex: We went sightseeing all morning.
Abbiamo fatto giri turistici tutta la mattina.
I bought a small souvenir for my sister.
Ho comprato un piccolo souvenir per mia sorella.
The journey from Turin to Paris was long.
Il viaggio da Torino a Parigi è stato lungo.
words.note: «Journey» è lo spostamento da un luogo a un altro; il viaggio come vacanza è trip.

ex: She studied abroad for a year.
Ha studiato all'estero per un anno.
We checked in online before the flight.
Abbiamo fatto il check-in online prima del volo.
We got lost in the old town.
Ci siamo persi nel centro storico.

steps.s: We missed our connection because of a one-hour ___ .
steps.why: Dopo l'articolo serve un nome: delay. «Delayed» è aggettivo/participio, «late» è aggettivo.

steps.s: I forgot to ___ the hotel and everything was full.
steps.why: Dopo «to» il verbo è alla forma base.

steps.s: She bought a small ___ to remember the trip: a magnet from the market in Lisbon.
steps.it: Ha comprato un piccolo ricordo per la madre: una sciarpa dal mercato.

steps.s: We stayed in a very ___ hotel near the sea.
steps.why: Serve un aggettivo: comfort -> comfortable.
«Luggage» è non numerabile: niente plurale e verbo al singolare.

lessons.title: Una settimana a Lisbona
lessons.intro: Leggi il racconto di una vacanza con qualche imprevisto. Nota come i verbi al passato seguono la storia, dall'arrivo al ritorno.

steps.title: Lisbon, rain and sun cream
steps.text:
Last August my sister Chiara and I spent a week in Lisbon. We booked a small flat near the river because the hotels were too expensive. Our flight was late, so we arrived at midnight and I was so tired that I fell asleep in the taxi.

On the first morning we got lost. We were looking for a famous tram stop when it started to rain, so we ran into a tiny café. While we were drinking coffee, an old man at the next table showed us the way on his phone. He was very kind and he even told us about a restaurant that tourists never visit.

The best day was Wednesday. We took a train to the seaside and spent the whole afternoon on the beach. I forgot my sun cream and I came home with a terrible sunburn! Chiara laughed at me while I was putting yoghurt on my back. In the evening we ate grilled fish and listened to live music in the street.

On the last day we bought some souvenirs for our parents. At the airport I couldn't find my passport for ten minutes, but it was in my coat pocket all the time. I loved Lisbon and I want to go back next year, but this time with sun cream.

qs.q: Why did the sisters book a flat?
What time did they arrive in Lisbon?
What did they do when it started to rain?
opts: They went back to the flat.

qs.q: The old man gave them a paper map.
qs.why: Ha mostrato la strada sul telefono, non con una mappa di carta.

qs.q: They went to the seaside by ___ .
What happened to the writer on Wednesday?
qs.why: «...I came home with a terrible sunburn».

qs.q: Where was the writer's passport at the airport?
qs.why: «...it was in my coat pocket all the time».

qs.q: The writer would like to visit Lisbon again.
qs.why: «I want to go back next year».

steps.s: We were so tired that we ___ asleep in the taxi.
steps.why: Fall asleep = addormentarsi; il past simple di fall è fell («felt» è il passato di feel).

steps.q: Trova nel testo la parola che significa «lungo il mare»
steps.text: We took a train to the ___ .

lessons.title: Com'è andato il weekend?
lessons.intro: Due colleghi chiacchierano il lunedì mattina davanti alla macchinetta del caffè. Ascolta senza leggere: il testo lo vedi solo alla fine.

steps.title: Monday morning
steps.it: Ascolta il dialogo e rispondi. Puoi riascoltarlo e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Morning, Sofia. Did you have a good weekend?
Yes, thanks! We went to the lake with my cousins. On Saturday we hired a boat.
Well, it was sunny in the morning, but it started to rain while we were having lunch. We all ran back to the car.
Oh no! What did you do then?
We found a little restaurant and stayed there until six. Actually, it was the best part. And you? Did you do anything?
Not much. I stayed at home on Saturday and painted the kitchen. Then on Sunday I met my brother for a walk.
Did you paint it yellow, like you wanted?
No, I changed my mind in the shop and bought blue paint.
Blue is nice! Anyway, the coffee is ready. Shall we go?

qs.q: Where did Sofia go at the weekend?
What did Sofia and her cousins do on Saturday?
What were they doing when it started to rain?
How long did they stay in the restaurant?
What did Ben do on Saturday?
What did Ben do on Sunday?

steps.en: It started to rain while we were having lunch.
steps.it: Ha iniziato a piovere mentre pranzavamo.

steps.en: I changed my mind in the shop and bought blue paint.
steps.it: Ho cambiato idea in negozio e ho comprato la vernice blu.

steps.en: Did you have a good weekend?
steps.it: Hai passato un bel weekend?

lessons.title: Raccontare il weekend a un collega
lessons.intro: Il lunedì mattina in ufficio ti chiedono com'è andato il weekend. Frasi per raccontare, reagire a quello che senti e far procedere la conversazione.

steps.title: Chiedere e raccontare
steps.body:
Per chiedere:
- **How was your weekend?** / **Did you have a good weekend?**
- **Did you do anything nice?**
- **Where did you go?** / **Who did you go with?**

Per rispondere:
- **It was great, thanks.** / **Not bad.** / **Pretty quiet, really.**
- **I went to... / We stayed at home and...**
- **Guess what happened!** = Indovina cosa è successo!

Non si dice «I have passed a nice weekend»: in inglese si **have** un weekend, e il tempo è il past simple: **I had a lovely weekend.**
ex: How was your weekend?
Com'è andato il weekend?
I had a lovely weekend.
Ho passato un bel weekend.

steps.title: Ordinare la storia e reagire
steps.body:
Per ordinare i fatti:
- **First, / Then, / After that, / In the end,**
- **On Saturday morning... / In the afternoon... / Later...**
- **While we were..., ...**

Per reagire a quello che ascolti:
- **Sounds great!** / **Lucky you!** = Che fortuna!
- **Oh no! What happened?**
- **What a nightmare!** = Che incubo!
- **Really? That's funny.**
ex: First we went to the market, then we had lunch.
Prima siamo andati al mercato, poi abbiamo pranzato.
Oh no! What happened next?
Oh no! Cos'è successo dopo?

steps.title: Al bancone del caffè
steps.it: Scegli la battuta più naturale per te (Tu).

opts: Great, thanks. We went to the mountains.
Great, thanks. We have gone to the mountains.
Great, thanks. We are gone to the mountains.

lines: Lucky you! Did you go skiing?

opts: No, we didn't. We just went for a walk.
No, we didn't went. We just walked.
No, we not did. We just walk.
Yes, it was freezing, but the views were fantastic.
Yes, it was freezing, but the views was fantastic.
Yes, it has been freezing, but fantastic views.

steps.title: Un weekend movimentato
lines: You look tired. What did you do at the weekend?

opts: I went to my friend's wedding. It finished at three in the morning!
I am gone to my friend's wedding. It finish at three in the morning!
I have gone at my friend's wedding yesterday.

lines: Wow! Did you dance a lot?

opts: Yes, I danced all night. I'm exhausted.
Yes, I did dance all night, I'm exhausting.
Yes, I dance all night. I am exhausted.

lines: What a night. Did you get home safely?

opts: Yes, a friend gave me a lift.
Yes, a friend gived me a lift.
Yes, a friend has give me a lift.

steps.why: «Exhausting» significa «che sfinisce»; «exhausted» è «sfinito». Un'altra differenza tra -ing e -ed.

steps.it: Che cosa hai fatto sabato sera?
steps.en: What did you do on Saturday evening
alts: On Saturday evening what did you do

steps.en: I had a lovely weekend, thanks.
steps.it: Ho passato un bel weekend, grazie.

steps.en: It started to rain while we were walking.
steps.it: Ha iniziato a piovere mentre camminavamo.
Oh no! Cos'è successo dopo?

steps.q: A colleague asks: How was your weekend? Tell the story.
steps.it: Racconta il tuo weekend (vero o inventato): dove sei stato, cosa hai fatto, un imprevisto con while o when. Almeno 4 frasi.
steps.model: I had a nice weekend. On Saturday I went to the market with my girlfriend and we bought some fresh fruit. While we were walking home, it started to rain, so we stopped in a café. On Sunday I stayed at home and watched a film. In the end I went to bed early.

lessons.title: Scrivere il racconto di una vacanza
lessons.intro: Scriverai un racconto breve di una vacanza, vera o inventata, poi lo racconterai a voce. Prima qualche esercizio per preparare connettivi e tempi verbali.

steps.title: Come si racconta una storia
steps.body:
Una storia breve ha:
- **un inizio**: Last summer I went to... / Two years ago we visited...
- **uno sviluppo** con i connettivi: **first, then, after that, later, while, when, but, so, because**
- **un imprevisto o un momento speciale**: Suddenly... / One day...
- **una fine**: In the end... / It was a fantastic holiday.

Regola d'oro: i fatti in ordine sono al **past simple**; lo sfondo (che tempo faceva, cosa stavate facendo) è al **past continuous**.
ex: We got lost while we were looking for the beach.
Ci siamo persi mentre cercavamo la spiaggia.
The weather was perfect, so we swam every day.
Il tempo era perfetto, quindi abbiamo nuotato ogni giorno.

steps.s: We wanted to visit the castle, ___ it was closed.
steps.why: Contrasto tra due idee: but.

steps.s: It rained all day, ___ we stayed at the hotel.
steps.why: Conseguenza: so.

steps.s: I met my husband ___ I was working in Dublin.
steps.why: While introduce un'azione in corso (was working); anche when è accettabile.

steps.s: Last year we have travelled to Spain with some friends.
answers: Last year we travelled to Spain with some friends
Last year we traveled to Spain with some friends
steps.why: Con «last year» serve il past simple, non il present perfect.

steps.q: Write a short story about a holiday you had (real or imaginary). Say where you went, what you did and what happened.
steps.it: Scrivi un racconto breve di una vacanza (vera o inventata): dove sei andato, cosa hai fatto, cosa è successo. Usa i tempi del passato.
checklist: Ho usato il past simple per i fatti, con almeno due verbi irregolari
Ho usato il past continuous con while o when almeno una volta
Ho usato almeno due connettivi (but, so, because, then)
Non ho usato il present perfect con un tempo preciso
Ho chiuso con una frase finale
useful: Then / After that / In the end
steps.model: Last summer I went to Croatia with two friends. We stayed in a small flat near the sea. On the second day we got lost while we were looking for a beach, but a friendly woman showed us the way. We swam, ate fresh fish and visited an old castle. The weather was perfect, except on the last day, when it rained. I bought a souvenir for my mum. It was a fantastic holiday.

steps.q: Tell us about the worst or best trip you ever took.
steps.it: Racconta il viaggio più bello o più brutto che hai fatto: dove, con chi, cosa è successo.
steps.model: The best trip I ever took was to Scotland two years ago. I went with my brother and we hired a car. We stayed in small villages and walked every day. One afternoon we got lost in the hills, but we found a farm and the farmer gave us tea. It was wonderful.

steps.q: Describe what you were doing at ten o'clock last night.
steps.it: Racconta cosa stavi facendo ieri sera alle dieci e cosa stavano facendo le persone intorno a te.
steps.model: At ten o'clock last night I was sitting on the sofa. My husband was reading a book and the children were sleeping. While I was watching a film, my sister phoned me, so I turned off the TV and we talked for half an hour.

lessons.title: Test dell'unità 2
lessons.intro: Verifica senza aiuti: grammatica, lessico, lettura e ascolto dell'unità. Le correzioni le vedi alla fine.

steps.title: Completa la cartolina
steps.text:
Hi Marco,

Greetings from Sicily! We {1} here on Tuesday after a long journey. The flight {2} two hours late, so we {3} dinner until eleven. While we {4} lunch yesterday, a cat jumped on our table! I {5} take many photos, because I forgot my camera.

See you soon,
Laura

steps.it: Ascolta il messaggio in segreteria.
lines: Hi Nina, it's Paolo. Sorry, I can't come on Saturday. I was in Naples last weekend and I lost my wallet on the train, so I'm going to the police station tomorrow. Can we meet on Sunday at four instead?
